gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, once CNET's measured fridge runtimes are rescaled from its efficient 54–60 W Whirlpool to a 585–679 kWh/yr full-size fridge, both 2 kWh picks (Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 and BLUETTI Elite 200 V2) fall to 21–24 h. Of the units with today's maker prices, the cheapest that still clears 24 h is the 3 kWh Jackery HomePower 3000 at 26.4–29.1 h for $1,499.
standout_why: I compared four rival pages. wattpowerstation.com (cited) relays CNET's runtimes, battery Wh used per fridge hour and fridge hours per $100. It gives CNET's fridge draw as 54–60 W but never rescales the runtimes to a bigger or older fridge. theoutagebrief.com (cited) only estimates runtimes, at a 1,260 Wh/day duty cycle with 85% efficiency, and says they are 'not measured results'. homepowerfacts.com (cited) applies a flat 80% (or its tested usable-Wh figure) to a 67 W fridge but does not use CNET's whole-run measurements. ChatGPT's answer quotes CNET's raw hours (27.40 / 26.32) as if they hold for any full-size fridge. No page points out that CNET's fridge (about 1.3–1.44 kWh/day) is smaller than a typical ENERGY STAR side-by-side (550 kWh/yr) or an older one (679 kWh/yr). None shows that the 2 kWh picks lose their 24 h margin on those fridges.
decides: It changes the pick. Under the optimistic fixed-overhead model, the C2000 Gen 2 and Elite 200 V2 clear 24 h only on an ENERGY STAR-level fridge (25.4 / 24.5 h at 550 kWh/yr). At 585 kWh/yr the Elite 200 V2 falls short (23.4 h) and the C2000 Gen 2 just reaches 24.2 h. On a least-efficient side-by-side (679 kWh/yr) both drop to about 21 h. For a guaranteed 24 h on an unknown full-size fridge, pick the Jackery HomePower 3000 ($1,499 on jackery.com today, 26.4 h even at 679 kWh/yr). The Anker SOLIX F3000 ($1,899.99, 24.3 h) clears the line only just. Keep the 2 kWh units for a shopper whose EnergyGuide label says about 550 kWh/yr or less.

findings.note: Relays CNET's July 2026 lab test of a full-size Whirlpool (118 V, rated 7.2 A). Conversion: 54 W × 24 h = 1.30 kWh/day and 60 W × 24 h = 1.44 kWh/day. The rescaling below uses the 57 W midpoint. I couldn't open CNET or the Yahoo syndication directly (blocked or 403).

findings.note: 550,000 Wh ÷ 8,760 h = 62.8 W; 679,000 ÷ 8,760 = 77.5 W. The page gives no data year (© 2015–). All the models it compares have icemakers.

findings.label: Rescaled runtime on 550 / 585 / 679 kWh/yr fridge
findings.source_title: Portable Power Station for a Refrigerator: Tested Run Times
findings.note: Fixed-overhead model: hours = Wh ÷ (Wh/h measured + (target W − 57 W)). 2,048 ÷ (74.7 + 5.8) = 25.4; 2,048 ÷ (74.7 + 9.8) = 24.2; 2,048 ÷ (74.7 + 20.5) = 21.5. This is optimistic because inverter loss also grows with load. Scaling the whole runtime by fridge watts instead (27.40 × 57/66.8) gives 23.4 h.
